provenance.note: Transcribed from CGWB 2025 Table 9.1 (GVMC's data; the same quantities as CGWB's June 2022 Table 5.1), the draft IFC Green City Action Plan that GVMC posted for public comment on 19 Oct 2024, GVMC's own NGT filings, and two Government of Andhra Pradesh filings in NGT Principal Bench OA 606/2018: the Chief Secretary's report of 10 July 2024 (present water supply, Annexure-VI) and the Feb 2026 affidavit (sewage figures). Table 9.1's other eight rows plus the low end of its Godavari/Yeleru range (182 of 182 to 204 MLD) are checked to sum to CGWB's printed 380 MLD total.

_note: No current source-by-source supply table from GVMC itself was found. The one used is GVMC's data as CGWB reports it, first in June 2022 (AAP 2020-21) and repeated unchanged in Nov 2023 and 2025.

hero_copy.headline: A port with no large river, drawing on the Godavari and Yeleru from up to {km} km away
hero_copy.body: {city} has no large perennial river of its own. Its largest source is the Godavari and Yeleru system, which CGWB lists at {km} km from the city; the water reaches the city through the Yeleru canal, a conveyance first built for the steel plant. About 380 MLD is available from nine sources, 182 to 204 MLD of it from this system (GVMC's figures; CGWB's tables carry the same quantities unchanged since its June 2022 report). That report said GVMC was able to draw 345.5 MLD of the 380, because of shortages at Raiwada and the Gosthani. We have not found a figure that splits the system's share between the two rivers. The canal is still shared: on 11 March 2021, the only day for which we have found GVMC's split, about 46 percent of the canal's tail-end water went to the city and 39 percent to the steel plant, with the rest to industrial parks, NTPC, rural water supply and the port.
hero_copy.wtp_sub: 11 plants (draft Green City Action Plan, Sept 2024)
hero_copy.uphill_sub: CGWB's distance for the Godavari/Yeleru source; the water comes by the Kateru pipeline and the Yeleru canal
hero_copy.pop_sub: GVMC's own estimate in its NGT filings (2021, 2024); no census since 2011
hero_copy.footer: Supply by source is GVMC's data as CGWB reported it in June 2022 and again, unchanged, in 2023 and 2025. Treatment capacity and litres per person from the draft Green City Action Plan that GVMC posted for public comment in Oct 2024. The canal split is GVMC's daily supply sheet of 11 March 2021, filed with the National Green Tribunal; the sheet prints no unit for the split, which is read as million gallons a day like its other columns. The draft plan puts water losses at nearly 30 percent (p30) and at 35 percent (p72) without saying how either was measured, and we have not found a measured non-revenue water figure for GVMC, so no losses figure is shown.

supply_chain: Godavari water lifted at two points: VIWSCO's Kateru pump house, into a 56 km pipeline to the Yeleru canal (since December 2004), and the Purushottapatnam lift, through the Polavaram Left Main Canal into Yeleru reservoir (since July 2018)
The Yeleru canal, about 150 km to the city (draft Green City Action Plan, p30), run with the Kateru pipeline by VIWSCO, a company GVMC and APIIC own
Shared at the tail end with the steel plant, NTPC, APIIC industrial parks, rural water supply and the port
Raiwada, Thatipudi, Meghadrigedda, Mudasarlova and the seasonal Gambheeram reservoirs, and infiltration wells on the Gosthani and Sarada
About 23 lakh people at 105 to 110 litres a person a day

_view_overrides.subtitle: GVMC's supply by source as CGWB has reported it since June 2022 (AAP 2020-21), unchanged in its 2023 and 2025 reports, with treatment capacity from the draft Green City Action Plan (2024). We have not found a newer source-by-source table from GVMC itself.

current_supply_mix_mld.source: Godavari and Yeleru, via the Yeleru canal
current_supply_mix_mld.scheme: VIWSCO conveyance to the Narava, Aganampudi and Gajuwaka plants
current_supply_mix_mld.note: CGWB gives 182 to 204 MLD for this source; its printed 380 MLD total matches the low end, so 182 is carried here. CGWB's 2022, 2023 and 2025 reports list the source at 190 km from the city. GVMC's supply sheet of 11 March 2021 prints 156 km against Yeleru reservoir and 56 km against the Kateru pump house; 56 km is the length of VIWSCO's pipeline from Kateru to the Yeleru canal, not a distance from the city. CGWB lists the source from 2005. The tail end of the canal is shared with industry (GVMC daily supply sheet, 11-03-2021, NGT OA 14/2021 (SZ) annexure).

current_supply_mix_mld.scheme: Raiwada water treatment plant at Narava
current_supply_mix_mld.note: CGWB 2025 gives 60 km; CGWB 2022 and 2023 give 56 km, and GVMC's 11 March 2021 supply sheet 76 km. An irrigation dam completed in 1981-82, with a city share carved out of it.

current_supply_mix_mld.scheme: Thatipudi, 10 MGD normal supply on GVMC's 2021 sheet
current_supply_mix_mld.note: 56 km (CGWB 2025 and GVMC's 2021 sheet; CGWB 2022 and 2023 give 60), in Vizianagaram district. Completed 1968.

current_supply_mix_mld.scheme: To the Mindhi plant, and raw water to the Naval Dockyard and MES (GVMC, 2021)
current_supply_mix_mld.note: 5 km (CGWB 2025); GVMC's 2021 sheet gives 20 km, and CGWB 2022 and 2023 write 'GVMC' in place of a distance. CGWB lists it from 1976; CWC's National Register of Large Dams (2019, as Mehadrigedda) gives completion in 1977, and GVMC's 2018 floating-solar IEE says constructed 1977, commissioned 1979.

40 km (CGWB 2025 and GVMC's 2021 sheet; CGWB 2022 and 2023 give 25). CGWB dates the source to 1930; press histories say Army Engineers built it in 1942. In July 1953 the Madras Assembly was told the Military Department had offered the Gosthani works to the Government for sale in 1946-47, at Rs 18.07 lakh, and that Rs 10 lakh was paid.
CGWB 2025 gives 20 km; GVMC's 2021 sheet lists 'Sarada River' at 40 km.
10 km (CGWB 2025 and GVMC's 2021 sheet). The town's first water works, handed over in May 1903 (Francis, Vizagapatam District Gazetteer, 1907).
30 km (CGWB 2025 and GVMC's 2021 sheet). Drawn seasonally.

_supply_total_note: CGWB states 380 MLD in Table 9.1 (83.67 MGD in its text) and 391 MLD in Table 9.3 of the same report; the draft Green City Action Plan (2024) gives about 395.5 MLD. Table 9.1's rows add to 380 to 402 MLD depending on the Godavari/Yeleru value (182 to 204); its printed 380 total matches the low end, so 380 and 182 are carried. 380 MLD also appears in CGWB's June 2022 and Nov 2023 reports, which call it the raw water available and say GVMC was able to draw 345.5 MLD of it. The Chief Secretary's report of 10 July 2024 in NGT Principal Bench OA 606/2018 (Annexure-VI, PDF p33) gives GVMC's present water supply as 334.03 MLD.

wtps_summary.note: 'Eleven water treatment plants with a total capacity of 489 MLD (107.46 MGD)' (draft Green City Action Plan, p30). No plant-by-plant list with commissioning years was found.

distribution.note: GVMC's own estimate ('about 23.00 lakhs') in its NGT filings of 2021 and 2024. The draft Green City Action Plan puts the distribution network at about 2,600 km.

allocation_context._lpcd_note: 'The per capita water supply, on average, is about 105 to 110 LPCD against the standard of 135 LPCD' (draft Green City Action Plan, p30). A city-wide average; the plan does not say how it was worked out.

_sewage.source_label: Government of Andhra Pradesh affidavit, NGT Principal Bench OA 606/2018 (Feb 2026), PDF pp71, 78
_sewage._note: Generation, installed capacity, utilisation and the gap are the state's own row for Visakhapatnam; reuse is '33 MLD (21%)', of which 25 MLD goes to the HPCL refinery. GVMC's own NGT affidavit of Mar 2024 (OA 40/2024 (SZ)) gives a different figure: it estimated generation at 215.05 MLD (85% of supply at 110 litres a person a day for about 23 lakh people). The later state figure is used.

groundwater._note: GVMC's supply sheet of 11 March 2021 lists 2.75 million gallons a day (about 12.5 MLD) from bores: 2.25 from 219 power-bore schemes and 0.50 from 8,224 hand bores. Both rows give the same figure for normal and present supply, so it reads as a set figure, not a reading. The draft Green City Action Plan (2024) says 30 percent of the city's water needs are met from groundwater. CGWB 2025 puts groundwater at 17.37 percent of supply, counting 30 MCM a year from its 2023 resource assessment against 142.71 MCM from surface water. No measured figure for how much groundwater the city draws was found.
